OMIM:612164.summary_plain: Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 4 is linked to changes in the STXBP1 gene. Research papers show these changes often make STXBP1 work less. That can disturb synaptic vesicle release, which helps nerve cells send messages.

steps.text: Records show STXBP1 causes this condition, with strong support from a curated disease link.
Research papers show many STXBP1 changes are loss-of-function changes. That means the gene makes less working protein, or the protein does not work well.
The same records also show STXBP1 is being studied in natural history and readiness studies. These studies may help families and doctors learn how this condition looks over time.
Some records suggest this condition looks similar to a few other childhood epilepsy conditions. That does not prove they share the same cause, but it may help researchers compare patterns.

uncertainties: The change effect is strongest for loss-of-function claims only. The records do not show gain-of-function evidence for STXBP1 here.
Several study links are marked as hypothesis or need verification. They should not be treated as fully confirmed assets.
The records do not show which exact STXBP1 changes cause which symptom patterns in this condition.
The records do not give treatment results for this condition, so benefit from any study is unknown.

next_step.text: Ask a doctor who knows genes to review the STXBP1 claims and the study records tied to this condition.

uncertainties: Some study links are marked as needing confirmation, so the exact match to this condition is not fully checked.

No treatment result for this condition is given here, and no asset row is fully verified in the input.
